purpose: Repaint the older judaism films reused in wave 1 so each has its own look (owner: "We can't have the same look for every film").
neighbours: new month-one Jewish films: 3 riso, 20 cutout, 29 woodblock, 30 impasto
rules: Never depict God in any form (God may only be suggested by light). Abraham, Moses and other prophets appear only from behind, in silhouette, or out of frame, never with a visible face.
today shots: Keep the people modern, diverse and real-looking.
each shot keeps its story beat and framing (the old still is uploaded as a layout guide); only the look changes

films.suffix: a Y2K chrome 3D render: liquid-metal surfaces, iridescent highlights, glossy bubble shapes, silver and lime reflections

shots.name: MZ1-Artaban-Pearl
shots.beat: Long ago, a great king named Artaban owned a pearl so fine that people said no one could put a price on it.

shots.name: MZ2-The-Gift-Arrives
shots.beat: He sent it to Rabbi Yehuda, the great sage of the Jewish people, with a message: “Send me something just as precious.”

shots.name: MZ3-The-Mezuzah
shots.beat: The rabbi sent back a mezuzah: a tiny scroll, written by hand, made to be fixed to the doorpost of a home.

shots.name: MZ4-King-Frowns
shots.beat: The king was offended. “I sent you something priceless, and you send me something worth a coin?”

shots.name: MZ5-Guards-At-Night
shots.beat: The rabbi answered: “You sent me something I must guard. I sent you something that guards you, even while you sleep.”

shots.name: MZ6-Today-Doorframe
shots.beat: today scene, today doorframe: today, as you leave home, rest your fingers on the doorframe for one second, the way people touch a mezuzah, and carry one good word out with you.

films.suffix: an ancient wall fresco on plaster: bold red and black panels, strong ochre and teal, crisp figures with dark outlines, fine cracks in the plaster, vivid not faded

shots.name: SH1-Two-Lamps
shots.beat: Friday, just before sunset. In a Jewish home, someone lights the lamps. When the sun goes down, Shabbat, the day of rest, begins.

shots.name: SH2-Walking-Home
shots.beat: The Talmud tells that on Friday night, two angels walk each person home from the synagogue. One good angel, and one bad.

shots.name: SH3-The-Lit-Home
shots.beat: If they find the lamp lit, the table set and the bed made, the good angel says, “May it be like this next Shabbat too.”

shots.name: SH4-Amen
shots.beat: And the bad angel, against his will, has to answer, “Amen.”

shots.name: SH5-Dark-Home
shots.beat: If the home is dark and nothing is ready, it goes the other way. The bad angel speaks the wish, and the good angel must say amen.

shots.name: SH6-Today-Candles
shots.beat: today scene, today candles: this friday, before the sun sets, light a candle on your table, and at dinner really look at the faces across from you. learn the blessing, or just watch the flame. your choice.

films.suffix: a woodblock print: carved line texture, two or three flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent

shots.name: SD1-Bricks-And-Mortar
shots.beat: In the book of Exodus, the Israelites are slaves in Egypt. Their lives are made bitter with hard work, with mortar and bricks.

shots.name: SD2-Night-Of-Leaving
shots.beat: After ten plagues, Pharaoh finally lets them go. And they leave in a rush, that very night.

shots.name: SD3-Dough-On-Shoulders
shots.beat: They carry their dough before it can rise, the kneading bowls wrapped in their cloaks, up on their shoulders.

shots.name: SD4-Flat-Bread
shots.beat: On the road, they bake it into flat cakes. There had been no time to wait. That flat bread is matzah.

shots.name: SD5-Seder-Table
shots.beat: Every spring, at the Passover seder, Jewish families tell it again. Seder means order, and the plate lays the story out as food.

shots.name: SD6-Youngest-Asks
shots.beat: Then the youngest stands up and asks: “Why is this night different from all other nights?”

shots.name: GL1-Wedding-Feast
shots.beat: The Talmud tells of a rabbi named Mar, son of Ravina, who made a wedding feast for his son, long ago in Babylon.

shots.name: GL2-Getting-Wild
shots.beat: The guests were great rabbis. And as the night went on, the celebrating got louder, and wilder.

shots.name: GL3-Precious-Cup
shots.beat: So Mar brought out a precious cup, worth a fortune, and held it up for everyone to see.

shots.name: GL4-The-Cup-Breaks
shots.beat: And in front of all his guests, he broke it.

shots.name: GL5-Quiet-Room
shots.beat: The room went still. The guests grew serious. The joy was still there, but now it remembered.

shots.name: GL6-Chuppah-Today
shots.beat: today scene, chuppah today: next time you celebrate something, even something small, take one quiet second for what’s still broken in the world, or for someone who isn’t there. then cheer.

films.suffix: a single graphic-novel comic panel: bold black inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angle, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering

shots.name: BM1-Judith-Morning
shots.beat: New York, 1922. A twelve-year-old named Judith Kaplan wakes up on a Saturday morning, a little nervous.

shots.name: BM2-The-Synagogue
shots.beat: Boys became bar mitzvah, “son of the commandment,” and marked it by reading from the Torah in synagogue. In most synagogues, girls had no ceremony like it.

shots.name: BM3-She-Reads
shots.beat: Her father, Rabbi Mordecai Kaplan, called her up. She said the blessings and read the week’s passage aloud, from a printed book, a little apart from the scroll.

shots.name: BM4-Faces-In-Pews
shots.beat: It became known as the first public bat mitzvah in America: “daughter of the commandment.” Some people were thrilled. Some were shocked.

shots.name: BM5-Today-Scroll
shots.beat: today scene, today scroll: do one mitzvah on purpose today. an easy, real one: call or visit someone who’s sick or alone. in jewish tradition that’s a mitzvah called bikur cholim, visiting the sick.

shots.name: BM6-Never-Too-Late
shots.beat: And some people mark it as adults, at thirty, sixty, even eighty. There’s no deadline.

films.suffix: a real frame grabbed from a 1990s music video on worn VHS tape, not a painting: heavy chromatic aberration, thick scan lines, tape noise and tracking glitches, oversaturated magenta and cyan, fisheye low-angle handheld camera

shots.name: HS1-Two-Schools
shots.beat: About two thousand years ago, two great teachers, Hillel and Shammai, each had a school of students. You met Hillel on day three.

shots.name: HS2-Three-Years
shots.beat: Their two schools argued about many things, from Shabbat to prayer. Once, they argued for three years, each side saying, “The law follows us.”

shots.name: HS3-Voice-From-Heaven
shots.beat: Then, the Talmud says, a voice from heaven spoke: “These and these are the words of the living God. And the law follows the school of Hillel.”

shots.name: HS4-Kind-Students
shots.beat: Why Hillel? Because his students were kind and humble. They taught Shammai’s view along with their own, and even taught Shammai’s first.

shots.name: HS5-Families-Together
shots.beat: And though they argued even about marriage law, the two schools still married into each other’s families. The argument never broke the friendship.

shots.name: HS6-Study-Partners
shots.beat: Today, many Jews study in pairs, arguing over a text across a table, out loud. It isn’t a lack of faith. It’s how people learn.

shots.name: AS1-Tent-Door
shots.beat: In the heat of the day, an old man named Abraham sat at the door of his tent. Three strangers appeared on the road.

shots.name: AS2-The-Meal
shots.beat: He ran to meet them and fed them: fresh bread, a tender calf, curds and milk. He stood by them under the tree while they ate.

shots.name: AS3-Above-Sodom
shots.beat: As the guests left, Abraham walked with them, looking down toward Sodom. Then God told him: the outcry against that city is great. I will go and see.

shots.name: AS4-Comes-Closer
shots.beat: Abraham came closer. “Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly?”

shots.name: AS5-Dust-And-Ashes
shots.beat: So Abraham kept going: forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, calling himself “but dust and ashes.” He stopped at ten. For ten, God said, I will not destroy it.

shots.name: AS6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: think of someone who isn’t in the room when things are decided about them. today, speak up for them once, kindly and directly. that’s how abraham did it.

films.suffix: a heavy impasto oil painting: thick palette-knife strokes you can feel, deep black-blue shadows, blazing highlights, dramatic chiaroscuro

shots.name: JW1-Coming-Home
shots.beat: Twenty years earlier, Jacob had tricked his twin brother Esau out of their father’s blessing, and run. Now he was coming home. Esau was coming too, with four hundred men.

shots.name: JW2-Alone-By-River
shots.beat: That night, Jacob sent his family and everything he had across the river Jabbok. He stayed behind, alone, in the dark.

shots.name: JW3-Wrestling
shots.beat: And a man wrestled with him until the break of dawn. No name. No warning. Just the two of them in the dust, all night long.

shots.name: JW4-Dawn-Hold
shots.beat: As dawn came, the stranger touched Jacob’s hip and wrenched it. “Let me go,” he said. Jacob answered, “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.”

shots.name: JW5-Limping-Sunrise
shots.beat: Jacob named the place Peniel, “the face of God.” The sun rose as he crossed over, and he was limping. Hurt, and renamed, in the same morning.

shots.name: JW6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: think of one struggle you’re in right now. today, write down one thing it has given you, next to what it has cost. jacob walked away with both: a limp, and a new name.

shots.name: SN1-Desert-Camp
shots.beat: In the third month after Egypt, the freed slaves camped at the foot of a desert mountain called Sinai. They were told to wash, to wait, and to keep back.

shots.name: SN2-Thunder-Cloud
shots.beat: On the third morning came thunder and lightning, a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of a horn growing louder and louder. The whole camp trembled.

shots.name: SN3-Into-The-Cloud
shots.beat: Moses climbed up into the cloud and came down again. Then, the Torah says, God spoke the Ten Commandments from the mountain, to the whole people.

shots.name: SN4-The-Answer
shots.beat: Moses read it all aloud, and the people answered together: “All that the Lord has spoken, we will do, and we will hear.” In Hebrew: na’aseh v’nishma.

shots.name: SN5-Two-Crowns
shots.beat: The rabbis tell that angels tied two crowns on each person, one for each word. And a voice from heaven asked, “Who revealed to my children the angels’ secret?”

shots.name: SN6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, try one small thing from these two weeks before you fully understand it: light a candle at dinner, or pause at a doorway on your way in. watch, learn or join in, it’s your choice. then notice what it tea

shots.name: JSC1-The-Question
shots.beat: The Talmud tells this. A Roman emperor asked Rabbi Yehoshua, “Why does the food you eat on Shabbat smell so wonderful?”

shots.name: JSC2-The-Answer
shots.beat: The rabbi smiled. “We have a spice,” he said, “and its name is Shabbat. We put it in the food, and that’s the smell.”

shots.name: JSC3-Give-Us-Some
shots.beat: “Give us some!” said the emperor.

shots.name: JSC4-Only-Works
shots.beat: “For anyone who keeps Shabbat,” said Rabbi Yehoshua, “it works. For anyone who doesn’t keep Shabbat, it doesn’t.”

shots.name: JSC5-Seventh-Day
shots.beat: The Torah says that on the seventh day God finished the work, and rested. Then God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy.

shots.name: JSC6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: this friday, or any day, pick one hour to stop on purpose: no work, no errands, maybe a candle and a slow meal. keep it in your own way. that’s where the spice comes from.

films.suffix: a loose watercolour and black ink wash on white paper: bleeding pigment, confident black ink linework, lots of white paper, one or two bold colours

shots.name: AP1-Two-Friends
shots.beat: The rabbis tell about Aaron, the brother of Moses. Whenever two people had quarreled and stopped speaking, Aaron went quietly to work.

shots.name: AP2-First-Tent
shots.beat: He sat with the first one and said, “Your friend is heartbroken. He keeps saying, ‘How can I face him? I’m the one who wronged him.’”

shots.name: AP3-Second-Tent
shots.beat: Then he went to the other one, sat with him, and said the very same thing.

shots.name: AP4-The-Embrace
shots.beat: When the two met, they embraced and kissed each other, friends again.

shots.name: AP5-Shalom-Door
shots.beat: The Hebrew word for peace is shalom. It comes from a root that means whole, complete, nothing missing. Jews say it for hello, for goodbye, and for peace.

shots.name: AP6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: think of two people near you who aren’t speaking, or someone you’ve drifted from. today, take one small step toward peace: a short message, or passing on something kind and true that one of them said about the

shots.name: SH1-Bedside
shots.beat: The Talmud tells this story. Jacob, the man renamed Israel, was very old, near the end of his life in Egypt. His twelve sons gathered around his bed.

shots.name: SH2-His-Fear
shots.beat: He had one fear. Would his children keep his faith after he was gone? Maybe one of them didn’t believe what he believed.

shots.name: SH3-Six-Words
shots.beat: His sons answered together: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is one. Just as there is only One in your heart, so in ours.”

shots.name: SH4-Whisper
shots.beat: And Jacob, at peace, answered softly: “Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.”

shots.name: SH5-Hand-Over-Eyes
shots.beat: Today, those six words, Shema Yisrael, are said morning and night. Many cover their eyes with one hand, to shut everything else out and just listen.

shots.name: SH6-Bedtime
shots.beat: Some children learn it as their first prayer, at bedtime. And tradition hopes it will be among the last words a person says, just like at Jacob’s bed.

films.suffix: a high-fashion editorial photograph, real models not a painting: sculptural styled wardrobe, dark seamless backdrop, a single hard spotlight, medium-format crispness, magazine-cover drama

shots.name: HN1-At-Shiloh
shots.beat: Every year, Hannah went with her family to the sanctuary at Shiloh. She longed for a child and had none. Year after year, she wept and couldn’t eat.

shots.name: HN2-Silent-Prayer
shots.beat: One year, she rose and went to pray alone. She spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved. Her voice could not be heard.

shots.name: HN3-Eli-Watches
shots.beat: The priest Eli was watching. He saw her lips moving, heard nothing, and decided she was drunk. “Put away your wine,” he told her.

shots.name: HN4-Not-Drunk
shots.beat: “No, my lord,” Hannah said. “I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink. I poured out my soul before the Lord.”

shots.name: HN5-Face-Lifted
shots.beat: She went on her way, and ate, and her face was no longer sad. In time, she had a son. She named him Samuel.

shots.name: HN6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: pick one thing you say on autopilot: a blessing, a prayer, or a plain “thank you.” today, pause for one breath before you say it, and aim your heart at the words. that pause is kavanah. which words you choose i

shots.name: JBZ1-The-Crowd
shots.beat: The Talmud tells of a rabbi, Ben Zoma. One day he stood high on the steps of the Temple Mount and looked down at a huge, busy crowd.

shots.name: JBZ2-A-Blessing
shots.beat: He said a blessing out loud: “Blessed is the One who created all these people to serve me.”

shots.name: JBZ3-Field-To-Bread
shots.beat: He explained. The first human had to do it all alone: plow, sow, reap, thresh, grind, sift, knead and bake. Only then could he eat.

shots.name: JBZ4-Ready-For-Me
shots.beat: “And I get up in the morning,” said Ben Zoma, “and find it all ready for me.” The farmer, the miller, the baker, the weaver. All of them.

shots.name: JBZ5-Two-Guests
shots.beat: He also said: a good guest says, “How much trouble my host took for me!” A bad guest says, “What trouble? I only ate one piece of bread.”

shots.name: JBZ6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, before your first bite of something, pause for two seconds. you could say a short blessing, in hebrew or your own words, or just think of one hand that brought it to you. watch, learn or join in, it’s yo

shots.name: JUK1-The-Doorway
shots.beat: In Babylonia, a rabbi named Mar Ukba had a poor neighbor. Every day, he slipped four coins into the socket of the man’s door, where no one would see.

shots.name: JUK2-Who-Is-It
shots.beat: One day the poor man thought, “I’ll go and see who is doing this for me.” So he waited by the door.

shots.name: JUK3-The-Oven
shots.beat: That day Mar Ukba was late from study, and his wife came with him. As the door opened, they ran and hid inside a baker’s oven, its fire just swept out.

shots.name: JUK4-Ladder
shots.beat: Centuries later, the great scholar Maimonides ranked tzedakah in eight levels, often pictured as a ladder. Giving in secret, so no one is ashamed, is near the top.

shots.name: JUK5-Top-Rung
shots.beat: And the top rung, above all the rest? Helping someone so they won’t need help again: a loan, a partnership, a job.

shots.name: JUK6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: find a jar, a cup, or a box. today, put in one coin, before you feel like it. when it’s full, give it away, quietly. that’s tzedakah, one coin at a time.

films.suffix: a hand-painted anime cel: clean ink lines, flat cel shading, lush painted backgrounds like a 1990s theatrical anime feature, huge skies

shots.name: JSP1-Twelve-Scouts
shots.beat: After the escape from Egypt, Moses sent twelve scouts ahead, one from each tribe, to explore the land of Canaan. They walked it for forty days.

shots.name: JSP2-The-Grapes
shots.beat: They came back carrying fruit: pomegranates, figs, and one cluster of grapes so big it took two men and a pole to carry it.

shots.name: JSP3-Grasshoppers
shots.beat: But ten of them said the cities were walled and the people were giants. “We were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

shots.name: JSP4-Two-Stand
shots.beat: That night, the whole people wept. Only two, Joshua and Caleb, stood up and said, “The land is an exceeding good land.”

shots.name: JSP5-Congregation
shots.beat: Later in the story, God calls those ten “this evil congregation.” The rabbis noticed: ten people were called a congregation. So ten became the smallest community in Jewish law.

shots.name: JSP6-Kaddish
shots.beat: Today, some prayers need a minyan of ten, like the reading from the Torah scroll and the mourner’s Kaddish. A mourner doesn’t say it alone. Nine others come.

shots.name: JNV1-City-Gates
shots.beat: God sent the prophet Jonah to Nineveh, a huge and violent city. Jonah ran the other way, onto a ship, and into the sea. But in the end, he went.

shots.name: JNV2-Warning
shots.beat: He walked into the city and cried out one short warning: “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”

shots.name: JNV3-Sackcloth
shots.beat: The people believed. They called a fast and put on sackcloth, rough cloth worn for mourning, from the greatest of them to the least.

shots.name: JNV4-The-King
shots.beat: Even the king rose from his throne, took off his robe, and sat in ashes. “Who knows?” he said. “God may yet turn, and we will not perish.”

shots.name: JNV5-Morning
shots.beat: And God saw what they did, that they turned from their evil ways. And the disaster never came.

shots.name: JNV6-Neilah
shots.beat: Today, on Yom Kippur afternoon, the book of Jonah is read aloud. The whole community fasts together and says sorry in the plural: not “I have sinned,” but “we have.”

shots.name: JRL1-Jordan
shots.beat: The Talmud tells of Rabbi Yochanan, a great scholar, famous for his beauty. One day he was bathing in the Jordan River.

shots.name: JRL2-The-Leap
shots.beat: A bandit named Reish Lakish saw him and, in one great leap, jumped into the river after him.

shots.name: JRL3-Strength
shots.beat: Rabbi Yochanan looked at him and said, “Your strength should be for Torah.” Reish Lakish shot back, “Your beauty should be for women!”

shots.name: JRL4-Learning
shots.beat: He tried to go back for his things, and couldn’t. Rabbi Yochanan taught him, and he became one of the great sages of his time.

shots.name: JRL5-Teacher
shots.beat: Later, Reish Lakish himself taught: when a person turns back out of love, even their worst wrongs become merits.

shots.name: JRL6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: pick one small habit you’d like to turn from. today, try maimonides’ first steps: stop once, and say out loud, to yourself or someone you trust, what you’re turning from. that’s teshuvah, out of your head and i

shots.name: JEZ1-The-Square
shots.beat: Long ago, after years in exile, the people came home to Jerusalem. One autumn day, they all gathered as one, in the square before the Water Gate.

shots.name: JEZ2-Platform
shots.beat: Ezra the scribe climbed onto a tall wooden platform and opened the scroll in front of everyone. When he opened it, all the people stood up.

shots.name: JEZ3-Dawn-To-Noon
shots.beat: He read from early morning until midday. Men and women, and everyone old enough to understand, listened.

shots.name: JEZ4-Gave-The-Sense
shots.beat: As he read, the Levites, the teachers, stood among the people. They read clearly, and gave the sense, so the people understood the reading.

shots.name: JEZ5-Go-Eat
shots.beat: The people began to weep. But they were told: don’t grieve. Go, eat rich food, drink something sweet, and send portions to anyone who has nothing ready.

shots.name: JEZ6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: look up this week’s torah portion: its name, and one line from it. that’s it. you’ve just stepped into a reading that has been going around the world for centuries.

shots.name: JBR1-The-Dark
shots.beat: The Torah opens with its first word, Bereshit: in the beginning. There was darkness over the deep, and the spirit of God hovering over the water.

shots.name: JBR2-Let-There-Be
shots.beat: Then God speaks, and that is all it takes. “Let there be light.” And there was light.

shots.name: JBR3-One-Day
shots.beat: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day.” Not “the first day.” One day.

shots.name: JBR4-The-Letters
shots.beat: The rabbis tell a story. The Torah begins with bet, the second letter. So alef, the first letter, came to God and complained, for twenty-six generations.

shots.name: JBR5-Sinai
shots.beat: God said: when I give the Torah at Sinai, I’ll begin with you. And the words spoken at Sinai begin with alef: Anochi, “I am.”

shots.name: JBR6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, notice one sentence before you say it, kind or sharp. choose the one that builds. that’s bereshit in a sentence: words make worlds.

shots.name: JLT1-Six-Days
shots.beat: In the Torah’s six days: light, then sky, then land and plants. Then sun, moon and stars. Then fish and birds. Then animals, and people.

shots.name: JLT2-No-Sun
shots.beat: But the rabbis noticed a puzzle. Light on day one, but no sun until day four. So what was that first light?

shots.name: JLT3-Edge-To-Edge
shots.beat: The Talmud says it was a special light. By it, the first human could see from one end of the world to the other.

shots.name: JLT4-Hidden
shots.beat: But God saw that later generations would do great harm. So God hid the light away, saved for the righteous in the time to come.

shots.name: JLT5-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: tonight, learn one line of torah, alone or with someone. a line from this week’s portion is perfect. a hasidic teaching says the hidden light was tucked inside the torah. then name one thing from today that was

shots.name: JHB1-Leaving-Class
shots.beat: You met the great teacher Hillel before. One day, as his class ended, he set off walking, and his students walked with him.

shots.name: JHB2-Where-To
shots.beat: “Rabbi, where are you going?” “To do a mitzvah,” he said, a holy deed. “Which one?” they asked.

shots.name: JHB3-Bathhouse
shots.beat: “To bathe in the bathhouse,” said Hillel. His students stared. “That’s a mitzvah?”

shots.name: JHB4-Statues
shots.beat: “Yes,” he said. “The statues of kings in the theaters: someone is paid to scrub and wash them, and is honored for it.”

shots.name: JHB5-Coins
shots.beat: The rabbis said it another way. A king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all look alike. God stamps every person with one seal, and not one is like another.

shots.name: JHB6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, do one small thing to care for your body, a walk, a glass of water, an early night, and tell yourself: i’m taking care of the image. jews even say a short blessing, asher yatzar, thanking god for a body

shots.name: MN1-Hungry-Desert
shots.beat: In the desert after Egypt, the freed slaves were hungry. “In Egypt, we ate bread until we were full,” they grumbled.

shots.name: MN2-Like-Frost
shots.beat: So each morning, when the dew lifted, the ground was covered with something fine and white, like frost. “What is it?” they asked. In Hebrew, man hu. Manna.

shots.name: MN3-Gathering
shots.beat: Everyone gathered what they needed for the day. Some gathered more, some less, and yet no one had too much, and no one had too little.

shots.name: MN4-Double-Portion
shots.beat: On the sixth day, there was twice as much. Moses told them: tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Shabbat. Bake what you need today.

shots.name: MN5-Empty-Ground
shots.beat: On the seventh day, some went out anyway with their baskets. They found nothing. So the people rested on the seventh day.

shots.name: MN6-Two-Loaves
shots.beat: Today, many Jewish families set two loaves of challah on the Shabbat table, under a cloth. Two loaves, for the double bread before that first rest.

films.suffix: a layered paper cut-out collage: cut and torn coloured paper, visible paper fibres, soft drop shadows, handmade diorama depth, bright lime, pink, saffron and turquoise paper

shots.name: JPK1-Dust
shots.beat: In the Torah, God forms the first human from the dust of the ground. The ground is adamah. The human made from it is adam: the earthling.

shots.name: JPK2-Breath
shots.beat: Then God breathes into his nostrils the breath of life, “and man became a living soul.” Earth and breath, in one person.

shots.name: JPK3-The-Rebbe
shots.beat: In Poland, about two hundred years ago, a Hasidic teacher, Rabbi Simcha Bunim, told his students: everyone should have two pockets.

shots.name: JPK4-Two-Slips
shots.beat: One slip says, “For my sake the world was created,” a saying of the rabbis. The other has Abraham’s words: “I am but dust and ashes.”

shots.name: JPK5-Which-One
shots.beat: When you feel too proud, reach for the dust. When you feel worthless, reach for the other pocket. The trick, he said, is knowing which one.

shots.name: JPK6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, write the two lines on two small slips of paper, one for each pocket. when the day lifts you too high or pushes you too low, reach in. which line you need is up to you.

films.suffix: a hand-painted anime cel: clean ink lines, flat cel shading, lush painted backgrounds like a 1990s theatrical anime feature, huge skies

shots.name: JHO1-Carob
shots.beat: The Talmud tells of Honi, a holy man. One day he saw an old man planting a carob tree. “How long until it gives fruit?” he asked. “Seventy years.”

shots.name: JHO2-Sleep
shots.beat: Honi sat down to eat, and sleep came over him. Rocks rose up around him, hiding him from view, and he slept for seventy years.

shots.name: JHO3-Grandson
shots.beat: When he woke, a man was picking carobs from the tree. “Did you plant this?” Honi asked. “No, my grandfather did.”

shots.name: JHO4-Study-Hall
shots.beat: Honi went to the study hall. He heard the scholars say, “These teachings are as clear as in the days of Honi.” “I am Honi!” he said. No one believed him.

shots.name: JHO5-Either
shots.beat: Heartbroken, Honi prayed for mercy, and his life came to an end. That, the Talmud says, is the old saying: either friendship, or death.

shots.name: JHO6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: today, ask one person to learn something with you: a chapter, a recipe, a song. that’s chavruta, friendship out loud. or simply call someone who really knows you.

films.suffix: a loose watercolour and black ink wash on white paper: bleeding pigment, confident black ink linework, lots of white paper, one or two bold colours

shots.name: JAY1-The-Fruit
shots.beat: In the garden, the first man and woman ate from the one tree they were told to leave alone. The text never says apple. Just fruit.

shots.name: JAY2-Hiding
shots.beat: Their eyes were opened. They sewed fig leaves together, and when they heard God in the garden in the cool of the day, they hid among the trees.

shots.name: JAY3-Ayekah
shots.beat: And God called to the man, “Where art thou?” In Hebrew, it’s one word: ayekah.

shots.name: JAY4-The-Cell
shots.beat: Long after, in a Russian prison, an official asked a jailed rabbi, Shneur Zalman: “If God knows everything, why ask Adam where he is?”

shots.name: JAY5-Every-Person
shots.beat: The rabbi answered: in every age, God calls to every person, “Where are you in your world? So many years of your life have passed. Where are you?”

shots.name: JAY6-Today
shots.beat: today scene, today: tonight, ask yourself the one-word question: ayekah, where am i? answer in one honest sentence, no blame, no excuses. write it down if you like.
